chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad narrated to me from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Abdillah ibn Hilal, from Uqbah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), in his long hadith, who said:

Then you will pass by the grave of Hamzah ibn Abd al-Muttalib and greet him, then you will pass by the graves of the martyrs and stand by them and say: Peace be upon you, O inhabitants of the dwellings. You have preceded us and we shall be following you.

Then you will come to the mosque that is in the wide place beside the mountain on your right, until you enter Uhud and pray in it. At that place, the Prophet (peace be upon him) went out to Uhud where he met the polytheists, and they did not depart until the prayer time arrived, so he prayed in it.
Then you will pass by again until you return, and pray by the graves of the martyrs as much as Allah has written for you.

Then proceed on your way until you come to the Mosque of the Confederates (Masjid al-Ahzab) and pray in it, for the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) supplicated in it on the Day of the Confederates.

And he said: O Helper of the distressed, O Answerer of the call of the afflicted, O Aid of the anxious! Remove my worry, my anguish, and my sadness, for You see my state and the state of my companions.

key_terms.قَبْرُ حَمْزَ: The grave of Hamzah ibn Abd al-Muttalib
key_terms.يَوْمَ الْأَحْزَابِ: The Day of the Confederates (Battle of Khandaq)

ai.seo_question: What is the recommended sequence of visiting martyrs' graves and mosques at Uhud according to Shia tradition?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (a.s.) establishes a structured spiritual itinerary for visiting the martyrs of Uhud, emphasizing the concept of *al-farṭ* (pioneers) where the living follow the path of the dead. It highlights the continuity of prophetic legacy by linking the visitation of Hamzah and the Uhud martyrs with the specific mosques where the Prophet prayed and supplicated during key historical events like the Battle of the Confederates. This ritual serves not only as a commemoration but as a means of drawing spiritual proximity to the Ahl al-Bayt through the intercession of the early martyrs.
